name: Mark Knopfler
milestone_by_age_26: Ineligible: Knopfler was a part-time English teacher and struggling musician through his mid-twenties; he formed Dire Straits in 1977 at age 28 and released the debut album in 1978 at age 29. No material milestone by age 26 found.
early_history_summary: Knopfler was inspired by his uncle's harmonica and boogie-woogie piano playing as a child in Newcastle. He bought a guitar as a teenager and played in local bands, but pursued a degree at Leeds University and worked as a teacher and journalist before committing to music full-time. He formed Dire Straits in 1977 with his brother David, John Illsley, and Pick Withers.
family_context_summary: Born to an English mother who was a teacher and a Hungarian Jewish father who was an architect and chess player who fled the Nazis in 1939. Middle-class family in Newcastle.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was an architect; no direct music industry background in family. Uncle Kingsley played harmonica and boogie-woogie piano, inspiring early interest.
evidence_summary: Knopfler showed musical interest from childhood and played in bands as a teenager, but his career breakthrough came late. He was a teacher and journalist through his twenties, forming Dire Straits at age 28 in 1977. His first album was released in 1978 at age 29, with the hit 'Sultans of Swing' charting in 1979. No material, independently verifiable milestone occurred by age 26.

name: David Beckham
milestone_by_age_26: Won the FA Youth Cup with Manchester United's Class of '92 in May 1992 and made his first-team debut on 23 September 1992 at age 17, launching a career that by age 26 included six Premier League titles, two FA Cups, and the 1999 UEFA Champions League.
early_history_summary: Beckham signed schoolboy forms with Manchester United on his 14th birthday in 1989 and a YTS contract in July 1991. He was part of the Class of '92 that won the FA Youth Cup, scoring in the final. He made his first-team debut as a substitute in a League Cup match in September 1992 and signed professional terms in January 1993. He became a first-team regular by 1995-96 and a global star by the late 1990s.
family_context_summary: Son of Sandra (née West), a hairdresser, and David Edward Alan 'Ted' Beckham, a kitchen fitter. Working-class family in Leytonstone, London. Parents were fanatical Manchester United supporters who travelled 200 miles to home matches.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father coached Beckham's local youth team Ridgeway Rovers and was a devoted Manchester United fan, providing direct football immersion from childhood. No professional football background in family.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Manchester United academy, Class of 92, father-coached youth team, Eric Harrison mentor
evidence_summary: Beckham was immersed in football from childhood by his fanatical Manchester United-supporting parents, with his father coaching his local youth team. He joined Manchester United's academy at 14, was coached by Eric Harrison alongside the Class of '92 (Giggs, Scholes, Neville, Butt), won the FA Youth Cup at 17, and made his first-team debut the same year. The elite academy pipeline and exceptional peer group were the dominant early advantages. By age 26 he had won six Premier League titles and the Champions League.

name: Alain Connes
milestone_by_age_26: Ineligible: Connes completed his PhD thesis 'A Classification of Factors of Type III' in 1973 at age 26, which is standard timing for a French ENS graduate. His first major recognition (Aimé Berthé Prize) came in 1975 at age 28, the Peccot-Vimont Prize in 1976, and the Fields Medal in 1982 at age 35. No material, independently verifiable recognition milestone occurred by age 26.
early_history_summary: Connes attended Lycée Saint-Charles in Marseille and classes préparatoires at Lycée Thiers before entering the École Normale Supérieure in Paris in 1966 at age 19. He became a CNRS researcher from 1970 to 1975 and completed his PhD under Jacques Dixmier in 1973. His thesis on operator algebras was significant but its recognition came after age 26.
family_context_summary: Born in Draguignan, near Cannes, France. Family background not documented in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Connes entered the elite École Normale Supérieure at 19 and completed his PhD at 26 under Jacques Dixmier. While his thesis on type III factors was mathematically significant, the material recognition (Aimé Berthé Prize 1975, Peccot-Vimont Prize 1976, CNRS Silver Medal 1977, Fields Medal 1982) all came after age 26. A PhD at 26 is standard timing for an ENS graduate and does not constitute a material milestone of success by that age.

name: Hans Zimmer
milestone_by_age_26: Composed his first film score for 'Moonlighting' (1982), a Palme d'Or-nominated Channel 4 film, at age 24-25, and co-founded Lillie Yard Studio with film composer Stanley Myers that same year.
early_history_summary: Zimmer was largely self-taught, playing piano from age 3 but rejecting formal lessons. Inspired by Ennio Morricone's score for 'Once Upon a Time in the West' at around age 12, he moved to London as a teenager. He wrote advertising jingles for Air-Edel Associates in the mid-1970s, played keyboards with the Buggles (appearing in the 'Video Killed the Radio Star' video in 1979), and worked with various new wave bands. He found a mentor in film composer Stanley Myers, with whom he co-founded Lillie Yard Studio and began working on film scores in 1982.
family_context_summary: Born in Frankfurt, West Germany. Father died when Zimmer was six years old, which intensified his commitment to music. Mother was a classically trained pianist who facilitated a musical environment. He attended boarding school in Switzerland before moving to London as a teenager.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother was a classically trained pianist who created a musical home environment. Father encouraged his innovative approach to music before his death when Zimmer was six. No film industry connections in family.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Stanley Myers mentorship, self-taught, London music scene, Morricone inspiration, early father death
evidence_summary: Zimmer was a self-taught musician inspired by Morricone's film scores from age 12. After his father's death when he was six, music became his refuge. He moved to London as a teen, wrote jingles, played in bands including the Buggles, and found a pivotal mentor in film composer Stanley Myers. Together they founded Lillie Yard Studio in 1982, and Zimmer composed his first film score for 'Moonlighting' that year at age 24-25. His breakthrough with 'Rain Man' came later in 1988 at age 31, but the first film score and studio founding represent a material milestone by 26.

name: Arturo Merzario
milestone_by_age_26: Won the European Tourism Championship and the Mugello Grand Prix in 1969 at age 26, driving an Abarth, which earned him a call to the Ferrari factory sportscar team for 1970.
early_history_summary: Merzario ran his first race in 1962 at age 19 with Scuderia Lario at Monza, driving his brother's car. He was hired by Abarth as a test and racing driver, building a reputation in small-capacity sports cars and hill climbs. In 1969 he won the Mugello Grand Prix and the European Tourism Championship, which led to his recruitment by Ferrari for their sportscar team in 1970. He made his Formula One debut in 1972 at age 29.
family_context_summary: Son of a successful building contractor from Como, Italy. Family had sufficient resources to support early racing, with his parents giving him a Giulietta Spider 1300 for racing.
parent_family_domain_summary: No racing background in family. Father was a building contractor who provided financial means for early racing but no domain expertise.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Abarth factory team, Italian motorsport, family financial support, early racing at 19
evidence_summary: Merzario began racing at 19 in 1962, using his brother's car and later a Giulietta Spider 1300 from his parents. His father, a building contractor, provided financial support. He was hired by Abarth as a test and racing driver, building expertise in sports cars through the 1960s. In 1969 at age 26, he won the European Tourism Championship and the Mugello Grand Prix, earning a Ferrari factory drive for 1970. His natural driving talent and early immersion in Italian motorsport were key advantages.

name: Paco de Lucía
milestone_by_age_26: Released his first solo album 'La fabulosa guitarra de Paco de Lucía' in 1967 at age 19, and won the first prize at the Concurso Nacional de Arte Flamenco in Córdoba in 1968 at age 20, establishing himself as a leading flamenco guitarist.
early_history_summary: Born in Algeciras, Spain, to flamenco guitarist Antonio Sánchez Pecino and Portuguese mother Lúcia Gomes, Paco began playing guitar at age 5 under his father's strict guidance, practicing up to 12 hours daily. He made his first public appearance on Radio Algeciras at age 11 in 1958, won a special prize at the Jerez flamenco competition at 11, recorded his first record with his brother Pepe at 14, toured the US with José Greco's dance company at 14-15, and made his first solo recording at 16. His first solo album came at 19 and the national flamenco competition win at 20.
family_context_summary: Youngest of five children of flamenco guitarist Antonio Sánchez Pecino and Portuguese mother Lúcia Gomes. Working-class family in Algeciras. Father was extremely strict, forcing up to 12 hours of daily practice and eventually taking Paco out of school to focus solely on guitar.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a flamenco guitarist who received guitar lessons himself and introduced Paco to the guitar at age 5. Father's relationship with Paco was compared to Leopold Mozart and Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart in the way he moulded his son into a world-class musician. Brothers Pepe (singer) and Ramón (guitarist) were also professional flamenco musicians.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Father as flamenco guitarist mentor, 12 hours daily practice, Andalusian flamenco heartland, brothers as musical peers, child prodigy, taken out of school
evidence_summary: Paco de Lucía's father, flamenco guitarist Antonio Sánchez Pecino, introduced him to the guitar at age 5 and enforced up to 12 hours of daily practice, eventually removing him from school to focus solely on music. This Mozart-like apprenticeship produced a virtuoso who made his radio debut at 11, recorded at 14, toured internationally at 14-15, released his first solo album at 19, and won the national flamenco competition at 20. The family-domain apprenticeship in the flamenco heartland of Andalusia, with brothers Pepe and Ramón as musical peers, was the dominant early advantage.

name: Giuseppe Sinopoli
milestone_by_age_26: Obtained his doctorate in medicine (psychiatry) from the University of Padua in 1972 and was appointed professor of contemporary and electronic music at the Venice Conservatory Benedetto Marcello the same year, at age 25-26.
early_history_summary: Sinopoli studied harmony and organ at age 12 in Messina, then harmony and counterpoint at the Venice Conservatory (1965-67). At his father's insistence, he simultaneously studied medicine at the University of Padua, graduating with a doctorate in psychiatry in 1972 with a dissertation on the physiology of sound perception. He also studied composition at the Accademia Musicale Chigiana in Siena under Franco Donatoni (1969-73) and attended Darmstadt courses with Stockhausen and Maderna. He became professor of contemporary and electronic music at Venice Conservatory in 1972, founded the Bruno Maderna Ensemble in 1975, and made his conducting debut at the Royan Festival that year.
primary_leverage_engine: Dual expertise in medicine and music
family_context_summary: Born in Venice, Italy. Father insisted he study medicine alongside music. Family financial background not documented in reviewed sources.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father's insistence on medical studies provided a dual-track education but no direct music domain advantage. Family supported both medical and musical education simultaneously.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Venice Conservatory, University of Padua, Darmstadt, Stockhausen and Maderna mentors, dual medicine-music track
evidence_summary: Sinopoli pursued an unusual dual track in medicine and music, studying at the Venice Conservatory and the University of Padua simultaneously. By age 25-26 in 1972, he held both a doctorate in psychiatry and a professorship in contemporary and electronic music at the Venice Conservatory. He was mentored by avant-garde composers Bruno Maderna and Franco Donatoni and attended the elite Darmstadt courses with Stockhausen. His conducting career began later, in 1975 at the Royan Festival, with his opera debut in 1977.

name: Patrick Tambay
milestone_by_age_26: Ineligible: Tambay started racing relatively late at age 23 in 1971. By age 26 (June 1975), he had won the Pilote Elf scholarship (1973) and competed in European Formula 2 (1974), but his material success — the Can-Am championship (1977) and Formula One debut (1977) — came after age 26. No material milestone of success by age 26 found.
early_history_summary: Tambay was a skilled junior skier who won the French national junior downhill title at 18 and attended the University of Colorado on a skiing scholarship. He started racing at age 23 in 1971 after attending a racing school at Paul Ricard. He won the Pilote Elf scholarship in 1973, was runner-up in the European Formula Renault Championship, moved to F2 in 1974, and won the Can-Am championship in 1977 at age 28 before entering Formula One.
family_context_summary: Born in Paris, son of a building developer who moved to the Côte d'Azur. Family had sufficient means for skiing and international education. Tambay attended university in Colorado on a skiing scholarship.
parent_family_domain_summary: No racing background in family. Father was a building developer, providing a comfortable upbringing but no motorsport connections.
evidence_summary: Tambay started racing at the relatively late age of 23 in 1971 after a skiing background. He won the Pilote Elf scholarship in 1973 and competed in F2 in 1974, but his material racing success — the Can-Am championship and Formula One debut — both came in 1977 at age 28, after age 26. No material, independently verifiable milestone of success occurred by age 26.

name: Riccardo Muti
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Guido Cantelli International Conducting Competition in Milan in 1967 by unanimous jury vote at age 25-26, and was appointed principal conductor and music director of the Maggio Musicale Fiorentino in 1968 at age 26-27.
early_history_summary: Born in Naples, Muti studied piano under Vincenzo Vitale at the Conservatory of San Pietro a Majella, graduating with distinction. He then received a diploma in composition and conducting from the Giuseppe Verdi Conservatory in Milan under Bruno Bettinelli and Antonino Votto, also studying composition with Nino Rota. His breakthrough came when he won the Cantelli Competition unanimously in 1967, leading immediately to the Florence appointment. He was invited by Karajan to the Salzburg Festival in 1971 and became chief conductor of the London Philharmonia in 1972.
family_context_summary: Born in Naples, spent early childhood in Molfetta, near Bari. Father Domenico was a pathologist and amateur singer and great music lover. Mother Gilda was a reserved Neapolitan woman. Middle-class family with five children. Father supported musical education.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a pathologist who was also an amateur singer and passionate music lover, providing early musical exposure. No professional music background, but father's love of music directed Muti toward musical training from a young age.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Naples and Milan conservatories, Cantelli Competition, Antonino Votto and Nino Rota mentors, father's musical passion
evidence_summary: Muti was immersed in music from childhood by his pathologist father who was an amateur singer and music lover. He trained at two elite Italian conservatories — San Pietro a Majella in Naples and Giuseppe Verdi in Milan — studying under notable mentors including Antonino Votto and Nino Rota. His unanimous win of the Cantelli Conducting Competition in 1967 at age 25-26 was a decisive breakthrough, immediately leading to the principal conductorship of the Maggio Musicale Fiorentino. The elite institutional pipeline and high-quality mentorship were the dominant early advantages.

name: Brian Jones
milestone_by_age_26: Founded the Rolling Stones in 1962 at age 20, gave the band its name, and played their first gig at the Marquee Club on 12 July 1962. The band's first single 'Come On' was released in 1963 at age 21, and by age 26 the Stones were an internationally successful band with multiple hit albums.
early_history_summary: Born in Cheltenham to middle-class parents — father a piano teacher and aeronautical engineer, mother a piano and organ player — Jones showed musical aptitude early, becoming first clarinet in the school orchestra. He got a saxophone at 15 and a guitar at 17. He left home for London, became a blues musician calling himself 'Elmo Lewis,' and placed an ad in Jazz News in May 1962 auditioning musicians for a new R&B group. He founded the Rolling Stones, named the band, and was its initial leader and musical force before Jagger and Richards emerged as songwriters.
family_context_summary: Middle-class parents in Cheltenham. Father Lewis Blount Jones was an aeronautical engineer and piano teacher. Mother Louisa Beatrice played piano and organ and led the church choir. Both parents were of Welsh descent. Jones had two sisters, one of whom died of leukaemia as a child.
parent_family_domain_summary: Both parents were deeply musical — father was a piano teacher in addition to engineering work, mother played piano and organ and led the church choir. This provided a rich musical household environment, though no rock or blues connections.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Musical parents, London R&B scene, Jagger-Richards partnership, British blues boom, rebel outsider status, multi-instrumentalist
evidence_summary: Jones grew up in a highly musical middle-class household — father a piano teacher and aeronautical engineer, mother a church organist and choir leader. He became first clarinet in the school orchestra, got a saxophone at 15 and guitar at 17, then left for London to immerse himself in the blues scene. In May 1962 at age 20, he placed an ad for musicians and founded the Rolling Stones, naming the band and serving as its initial leader. The British R&B boom of the early 1960s and his partnership with Jagger and Richards were key structural advantages. His rebel disposition and bohemian lifestyle created urgency but also instability.

name: Mario J. Molina
milestone_by_age_26: Earned a BS in chemical engineering from UNAM (1965) at 22, an MS from the University of Freiburg (1967) at 24, and served as associate professor at UNAM where he established the first graduate program in chemical engineering (1967-68) at age 24-25, all before age 26.
early_history_summary: Born in Mexico City to a lawyer-diplomat father and a mother who managed the family, Molina was fascinated by chemistry from childhood, converting a bathroom into a home lab. His aunt Esther Molina, a chemist, mentored him with advanced experiments. At age 11 he was sent to boarding school in Switzerland to learn German. He studied chemical engineering at UNAM, then polymerization kinetics at Freiburg, and returned to UNAM as associate professor to establish the first graduate program in chemical engineering before pursuing his PhD at UC Berkeley (1968-1972).
primary_leverage_engine: Early chemistry immersion and family mentorship
family_context_summary: Father Roberto Molina Pasquel was a lawyer and diplomat who served as ambassador to Ethiopia, Australia, and the Philippines. Mother Leonor Henríquez was a family manager. Wealthy family that sent children abroad for education. Aunt Esther Molina was an established chemist who mentored Mario from childhood.
parent_family_domain_summary: Aunt Esther Molina was a chemist who provided direct domain mentorship, guiding young Mario through advanced chemistry experiments beyond toy chemistry sets. Father's diplomatic career provided international exposure and resources for education abroad. Family tradition of sending children abroad for education.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Aunt chemist mentor, home lab, Swiss boarding school, diplomat father, UNAM, early chemistry fascination
evidence_summary: Molina was immersed in chemistry from early childhood, converting a family bathroom into a lab and receiving mentorship from his aunt Esther Molina, an established chemist. His father, a lawyer and diplomat, provided the financial means to send him to boarding school in Switzerland at age 11. Molina earned his BS at UNAM by 22, his MS at Freiburg by 24, and returned to UNAM to establish the first graduate program in chemical engineering at 24-25 — a material academic milestone before age 26. His later Nobel Prize-winning CFC research came after age 30.

name: Bobby Moore
milestone_by_age_26: Made his West Ham United first-team debut on 8 September 1958 at age 17, earned his first England cap on 20 May 1962 at age 21, played in the 1962 World Cup, and became the youngest man ever to captain England on 29 May 1963 at age 22 — all well before age 26.
early_history_summary: Born in Barking, Essex, Moore joined West Ham United's youth setup in 1956 at age 15. He made his first-team debut at 17 in September 1958, replacing his mentor Malcolm Allison. He played for England youth teams, reached the FA Youth Cup final in 1959, and was called up to the full England squad in 1962 for the World Cup in Chile. He made his England debut against Peru in May 1962 and captained England for the first time in May 1963 at age 22, the youngest ever at the time. He went on to captain England to World Cup victory in 1966 at age 25.
family_context_summary: Son of Robert E. Moore and Doris (née Buckle) from Barking, Essex. Working-class family. Moore attended Westbury Primary School and Tom Hood School in Leytonstone, playing football for both. He was a talented junior cricketer as well, captaining South of England schoolboys.
parent_family_domain_summary: No football background documented in family. Moore was introduced to West Ham through a teacher, Tom Russell, who had connections with the club. No parental domain advantage in football.
primary_early_advantage_tags: West Ham youth academy, Malcolm Allison mentor, Geoff Hurst peer, East London football, game intelligence
evidence_summary: Moore grew up in a working-class family in Barking, East London, with no documented football connections. A school teacher connected him to West Ham's youth setup at 15, and he debuted for the first team at 17, replacing his mentor Malcolm Allison who was forced to retire by tuberculosis. Moore was not considered a natural prodigy — described as 'chubby' and 'sound rather than spectacular' as a child — but his exceptional game intelligence and reading of play set him apart. He earned his England cap at 21, played in the 1962 World Cup, and became England's youngest-ever captain at 22. He later captained England to World Cup victory in 1966 at age 25.
